`domcontentloaded`, never `networkidle`, on a dev server. Dismiss the consent banner first.
`Range.getClientRects()` gives per-line widths to *prove* a wrap point. **Mutation-test layout
fixes at mobile** — two fixes read as Δ0 at 1440 only because a taller sibling column masked
them.

**A design nudge is still spec.** Ship it and raise the question — don't silently "correct"
it, and don't silently ignore it. Document the deviation at the point of use.

### No automated gate in this stack catches a layout defect

`width: 'xl'` resolving to 576px destroyed the footer on every page while passing `tsc`,
`eslint`, `vitest`, local *and* remote CodeRabbit, and the Storybook a11y run. Only rendering
beside Figma found it.

---

## 6. Layout mechanics

Six mechanisms, each with the fix that actually worked.

1. **A wrapped element takes available width, not its longest line.** `width: min-content`
   resolves to the widest unbreakable run — usually what you want when a column should hug its
   longest word rather than its container.

2. **`minHeight` plus `align-items: center` loses leading when content wraps.** The centring
   discards the extra line's leading rather than growing the box. Derive height from
   `lineHeight` plus padding instead of reserving a `minHeight`.

3. **An inline child inside a block parent leaks descender space.** A block-level `<li>`
   wrapping an `inline-flex` `<a>` gets a line box whose strut sits below the baseline —
   measured **25.5px against the anchor's own 24px**, leaking 1.5px per row (3px on a wrapped
   label) and making the footer's links column 9px taller than Figma's 158px.
   **Fix: `display: flex` on the `<li>`**, which removes the line box entirely.
   `footerNavColumn.css.ts:69` is the shipped instance.
   ⚠️ `display: block` is the **bug**, not the fix.

4. **Give the gap to the heading, not the column.** If the design nests a group inside a stack
   with no gap, don't reproduce it as a sibling in a gapped flex container — the container's
   gap then applies where the design has none. Put the spacing on the heading's `marginBottom`.

5. **`flexWrap: nowrap` prevents breaking, not shrinking.** The row refuses to break, so the
   words break instead. This is what broke the unframed 768–1022 band.

6. **A non-breaking space must be the `\u00A0` escape**, not a literal character in source —
   invisible to review and unpredictable under reformatting. Note the dependency it creates:
   production copy has to carry the same character.

**A solution window measured in single pixels is a coincidence, not a tolerance.** The footer's
viable column cap was **[131, 132.9) — 1.9px wide**. Treat that as a signal the constraint set
is over-determined, not as a fix that happens to work.

## 7. Building against absent data

### Three patterns, only the first correct

**Guard, then render inert but perceivable.** Never render nothing where a control was
promised; never render a control that can't act.

- **An empty-string fallback is a layout bug** — `heading ?? ''` renders an empty element that
  **keeps its margins**, measured as a roughly 64px void. It doesn't collapse; it reserves
  space for nothing.
- **A silent element swap actively lies** — it promises an affordance that isn't there.
- **Fix at the atom**, not at each call site.

### The three-tier policy — the most reusable decision in the footer build

Behaviour differs by what the content *is*:

| Content class | Behaviour | Why |
|---|---|---|
| **Structural** (`footerConfig`) | render **nothing** — `if (!footerData) return null` | no fallback to placeholder once wired to live data, so an outage doesn't ship stale placeholder copy to real shoppers |
| **Microcopy** (`uiCopy`) | fall back to the **English literal** | losing a button label to an outage should never blank a control |
| **Per-item destination** (a contact href) | degrade **that item only** to a labelled non-interactive `<span>` | perceivable, but no false affordance |

The per-item case is the carefully argued one: no `href`, no `tabIndex`, so nothing promises an
action that cannot be performed (WCAG 2.4.4 / 3.2.4) — but **labelled, not `aria-hidden`**, so
a screen-reader user learns the channel exists instead of getting silence (avoiding the 1.1.1
information loss an earlier `aria-hidden` caused).

The same treatment is reused three times for "control with no action": the contact fallback,
`ZimmNavItem`'s no-href branch (renders a `<button>` that doesn't navigate), and `BottomBar`'s
locale placeholder (a `<div>`, deliberately not a `<button>`).

### Never branch on localised CMS text

`footerNavGroup` carries `showContactChannels: boolean` rather than matching
`heading === 'Contact'` — because `heading` is localised and silently stops matching the moment
an editor writes "Kontakt" or "Contacto". This footer ships to eight storefronts.

### Guarding hrefs

Every CMS-sourced href passes `isSafeHref` before reaching an anchor. The subtlety: WHATWG URL
parsing strips C0 control characters, tab, LF and CR *before* scheme detection, so a naive
`^javascript:` regex is bypassed by `java\tscript:`. **Normalise, then test.**

---

## 8. CMS data and the tier reality

New section. The footer rendered correctly in dev and was blank on the test tier, and nothing
in the component was wrong.

### Content types and entries promote by different mechanisms

| | Content **types** (schema) | Content (**entries**) |
|---|---|---|
| Mechanism | org-scoped Environment Template | *nothing automated* |
| Build | `npm run sync:contentful` | — |
| Deploy | `npm run install:contentful -- --target <env>` | — |

**A template cannot carry entries — this is structural.** The SDK type has exactly two slots:

```ts
// contentful-management/dist/types/entities/environment-template.d.ts:31-34
entities: {
    contentTypeTemplates: Array<ContentTypeTemplateProps>;
    editorInterfaceTemplates: Array<EditorInterfaceTemplateProps>;
};
```

No `entries`, no `assets`. The only entry-writing code in the repo is `seedRegions.mjs:71-72`,
which handles the 11 `region` entries and nothing else.

### Verified tier state, 2026-08-25

| tier | content types | published entries |
|---|---|---|
| **dev** | **14** | **42** (+3 assets) |
| test / sit / uat / staging | **0** | **0** |
| prod | no environment id configured | — |

The environments exist — the CDA returned `total: 0`, not `NotFound`. Nothing has ever been
promoted out of dev.

**The template covers 5 of dev's 14 types** — `footerConfig`, `footerNavGroup`, `link`,
`region`, `uiCopy`. The other 9 exist only inside the dev environment, UI-authored, with no
code representation, and `install:contentful` cannot move them.

**There is no forward content promotion in this repo at all.** The actual release model is the
alias flip in `promoteAlias.mjs`: clone master → install template → author and verify →
repoint `production`/`master`. Content moves *backwards* (master → clone), never forwards.

### Fetch-depth is load-bearing

`include: 3` is not arbitrary. At depth 2 the `regions` array arrives as unresolved stubs,
`region.fields.siteId` throws, the `.catch` swallows it, and the **entire footer renders
nothing**. A resolution-depth mistake looks identical to a network failure from the page.

### Locale is not passed on any Contentful fetch

`useContentful.ts:110` builds a URL with `content_type`, `access_token` and `include` only, so
the footer and `uiCopy` get the space default on all eight storefronts. Three invocation sites
across two production files. (`pages/experience/` and `pages/contentfulPreview/` *do* pass
`localeCode` — the gap is the shared hook, not every caller.) Blocked on a shared-
hook signature change, which is a team RFC.

### The check to run before promising a component works on a tier

```bash
curl -s "https://cdn.contentful.com/spaces/<space>/environments/<env>/entries?content_type=<type>&limit=1" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <that tier's delivery token>"
```

`total: 1` means it will render. `unknownContentType` means the model was never installed.
Note the CDA returns an unreliable `total` at `limit=0` — use `limit=1`.

---

## 9. Accessibility patterns

Six recurring success criteria and what each actually demanded.

- **1.1.1** — a degraded control must stay *labelled*, not `aria-hidden`. Silence is
  information loss.
- **1.4.4 / 1.4.10** — `rem` for anything that must survive zoom; a modal panel needs
  `maxHeight` + `overflowY` or tall content centres half-off-screen and is unreachable.
- **2.4.4 / 3.2.4** — no `href` and no `tabIndex` on a control that cannot act, so nothing
  promises an action that can't be performed.
- **2.5.8** — 24×24 minimum target size, which is a WCAG **2.2** addition and easy to miss if
  working from a 2.1 checklist.
- **2.5.3 Label in name** — the accessible name must *contain* the visible label.
- **3.2.5** — a link leaving the site gets `rel="noopener noreferrer"` and a suffix in its
  accessible name. That is the project's external-link standard; it lives nowhere else.
- **Focus** — a programmatic `.focus()` does **not** match `:focus-visible`. A focus ring
  styled only on `:focus-visible` will not appear after a scripted focus move.
- **Portal + focus trap** — when `activeElement` is outside the trap, the trap must handle it
  rather than assume containment.

Verification: what actually proves anything ### The integrity principle > The verification instrument was built from the same belief as the thing it verified, and was > never made to fail on purpose. That is the single recurring failure mode. A green check that was never proven capable of going red carries no information. Catalogued instances, all self-caught after reporting a false all-clear: a `safeHref` suite reported "well covered, 3 layers" whose 13 cases contained **zero backslashes** — the exact vector already named; a `fontFace` test iterating an empty array; a mutation test that "passed" because `perl -pi` works line-at-a-time and cannot match `\n`; a recipe parity check that false-alarmed three times on recipes whose `baseStyle` is a **function**; a literal-count sweep that inflated 19→41 by matching `.rem` inside `removeEventListener`. ### Copy the non-vacuity meta-test `recipeGuards.test.ts` includes `test('collect() actually walks the registered recipes')` precisely because every other guard asserts `toEqual([])`, which an empty input satisfies. Stubbing `components` to `{}` turned the whole file green — verified. Same shape for layout assertions: a pure before/after equality is satisfied vacuously by a collapsed container (`display:none`, `height:0`, an ancestor `display:none` — and every rect is 0 in jsdom). **Anchor the measurement above zero first.** And resolve a function-form `baseStyle` across **all** boolean prop combinations, not the default one. The original bug hid down a conditional branch a single-resolution walk never entered. ### Green tests that encode the bug A suite can test *around* a defect. The region tie-break suite had a case named "order of the tied candidates does not change the outcome" that used only **distinct** timestamps — the one arrangement already order-independent. It passed while the bug was live. Mutation testing is necessary but not sufficient: it proves the check *can* fail, not that it fails for the right reason. ### [CORRECTED] What is and is not gated **a11y IS gated.** An earlier belief — repeated four times in one session and again by a fresh analysis this week — was that a11y is ungated because there is no `.storybook/test-runner.js`. **That is Storybook 8 knowledge and is wrong for what is installed.** `@storybook/test-runner@0.24.4`'s `dist/setup-page-script.js:390-397` reads `story.parameters?.a11y?.test` and throws when it `=== "error"`; `.storybook/preview.tsx:44` sets exactly that. # FED Build Manual — Manual UI Build & Delivery

**Owner:** Marcel Navarro · **Started:** August 2026 · **Revised:** 25 August 2026

The developer-facing half. This is the sequenced procedure for taking a Zimmermann UI story
from session start to merged PR.

**Companions:** `uiBuild-knowledge.md` (why the machine behaves the way it does — read it when
something fails silently) · `fedLead-playbook.md` (the lead role: refinement, estimation,
review culture, escalation).

**Authority on styling:** `.claude/rules/overrideStyling.md`. If this manual and that file
disagree, **that file wins** — and tell me, because it means this one is stale.

---

## 1. The Operating Principles

### Static-first

Props in, markup out. A component under `overrides/app/components/` receives its data and
renders it. It does not fetch.

Mock data goes in the story — never a temporary fetch you intend to remove. A component that
owns its own data-fetching cannot be reused where the data arrives differently: SSR-prefetched,
mocked in Storybook, or composed by a parent that already has it.

**The one exception**, and it is narrow: Context-backed, app-wide static-content hooks
(`useIntl`, `useUiCopy`) may be called from any component, including a presentational leaf.
They read from a Provider mounted above the route tree, so they don't create the
SSR/Storybook/composition problem the rule exists to prevent. This covers content identical for
every consumer regardless of route — not anything that varies per page.

⚠️ **Their no-Provider behaviour differs and it will bite you in tests.** `useUiCopy` degrades
to fallback text and renders with zero setup. **`useIntl` throws**, and its `IntlProvider` is
mounted by the base SFCC `_app`, not `_app-config` — a narrower subtree than you'd expect. Any
Vitest test rendering a `useIntl` consumer must wrap it.

### Leverage what already exists

Four rungs, in order:

1. **Use the base SFCC component as-is.**
2. **Override it** — mirror the path under `overrides/`, keep the kebab-case filename.

**The default is override, not build — because an override inherits the wiring for free.**
Override `product-view` and you get `addToCart([{product, variant, quantity}])`, the
add-to-cart modal, bundle handling and `updateCart` already connected. And because the
resolver rewires imports transparently, overriding a component that SFCC's own base components
import means **the entire base template inherits your version with zero call sites touched**.

Worked examples: size selector → `swatch-group`; add to bag → `product-view`; max quantity →
`quantity-picker`; variant resolution → `use-controlled-variations` / `use-derived-product`.
Check what the base already does before scoping — a ticket saying "Cart API integration is in
scope" may be describing a call the base already makes.
3. **Compose existing ui-kit atoms** into something new.
4. **Build a new component.** Rarest. Justify it.

Before rung 4, check the registry (`.claude/registry/`) and grep `ui-kits/`.

**What `shared/ui` is actually for:** Contentful renderers need *primitives*, not commerce
components. Every Contentful component on `develop` already pulls them in — `duplexSection`
(`Box`, `Text`), `collectionHero` (`Box`, `Button`, `Heading`, `Text`), `hotspotPopup`,
`imageText`, `heroBanner`. Upstream those resolve to bare Chakra.

⚠️ **But the barrel is not the leverage play it looks like.** Overriding
`shared/ui/<Name>` to propagate branded styling into base cart/checkout/account **does not
work** — `shared/ui/index.jsx:29` re-exports relatively, which the resolver doesn't rewrite,
and 212 base files import the barrel (195 excluding tests) while **0** import the individual module. See
`uiBuild-knowledge.md` §4.

### Figma stays open the whole time

Not at the end. **And check the Jira card's Figma link actually points at your frame** — a
stale link propagates: you build the wrong thing, the BA signs off against a different frame,
QA tests a third source. If it's wrong, ask the BA to fix the card rather than working it out
in a DM.

There are **two Figma files** and cross-comparing them produces confident nonsense. See
`uiBuild-knowledge.md` §5.

### Ask in the group chat

Roughly 30 minutes stuck is the trigger. One question at a time.

### The bar you're building to

The SOW allows **10 defects, no Sev3** — the whole project, not per sprint. (Contract figure;
nothing in `.docs/` records it.) Expect UI PRs
to be reviewed against the preview environment **and** Figma. Self-review the same way before
you open it (§9) — it's faster than a review round-trip.

---

## 2. Before you write any code

### Confirm the branch

```bash
git branch --show-current
```

If it's `develop` or `main`, stop. No changes.

### Check what already exists

Read `.claude/registry/` for the component. The `Origin` column is what matters:

| Origin | Means |
|---|---|
| `Custom` | Zimmermann-authored, already here |
| `Override` | already mirrored into `overrides/` |
| **`Base`** | **still upstream — you pay copy-first** |

⚠️ **Do not trust the registry's `Tier` column.** `generateRegistry.mjs:125-203` hardcodes tier
arrays, lists no `ui-kits` path, and defaults everything else to Tier 4. Paths are reliable;
tiers are not. For what actually blocks, read `CODEOWNERS`.

### The three component families

| Family | Casing | Example |
|---|---|---|
| SFCC override | kebab-case, matching upstream exactly | `product-tile/` |
| **ui-kit component** | **camelCase — the default for new work** | `zimmButton/` |
| `shared/ui` primitive | PascalCase, mirroring upstream | `Button/` |

Kebab-case applies *only* to files mirroring a base Salesforce file. Naming a Zimmermann-
authored file in kebab-case falsely signals Salesforce origin — which inverts the convention's
whole purpose.

### Where a new component goes

```
overrides/app/components/ui-kits/{atoms,molecules,organisms}/<camelCase>/
  index.tsx
  index.stories.tsx
  <name>.css.ts          ← the recipe
  index.test.tsx         ← if it has branching or event wiring
```

**Tier by composition, read off the imports:**

- **atom** — imports no other ui-kit
- **molecule** — composes atoms, light local state
- **organism** — composes molecules/atoms **and owns domain state**

An icon passed as a prop doesn't count. Slotted children don't count.

### What's actually overridden today

Eleven directories:

```
_app-config  button  contentful  footer  foundation  header
icons  pageContainer  product-view  ui-kits  uiCopyProvider
```

Still base, despite being referenced throughout `.claude/rules/`: `product-tile`,
`display-price`, `swatch-group`, `image-gallery`, `link`, `list-menu`, `drawer-menu`, `seo`.
**Assume most stories pay copy-first.**

### The copy-first rule

For any task requiring an override that doesn't exist yet, prepare **all of them at once**
before any functional change:

1. Copy each file from `node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/` to the mirrored path.
2. Convert to `.ts`/`.tsx`, update imports.
3. `npx tsc --noEmit`.
4. Add a temporary `console.log('[overrides] product-tile.tsx')` to each.
5. **Stop.** Let the user confirm the overrides are rendering.
6. Remove the `console.log`s, then make functional changes.

Never bundle this silently with functional work.

---

## 3. Design Foundations

*The longest section, and the part that moves. Read it before your first component.*

### The styling hierarchy

1. **`textStyle`** for anything textual — `textStyle="body2"`, never a raw `fontSize`. All 22
   Handover text styles are registered:

   `heading1Strong` `heading1` `heading2` `heading3` · `body1Strong` `body1` `body2Strong`
   `body2` · `mobileBody1Strong` `mobileBody1` `mobileBody2` · `label` `caption` · `linkLg`
   `linkSm` · `button` `buttonSm` · `productNames` `price` · `navigation` · `footer` · `serif`
2. **`var(--zimm-*)`** for colour and spacing. The spacing scale:

   | | | | | | | |
   |---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
   | `3xs` 2px | `2xs` 4px | `xs` 8px | `s` 12px | `m` 16px | `l` 20px | `xl` 24px |
   | `2xl` 32px | `3xl` 40px | `4xl` 64px | `5xl` 80px | `6xl` 128px | `7xl` 160px | |

   Semantic colour groups in `foundation/colour.ts`: `background` (01–07), `text`, `border`,
   `status`, `link`, `icon`, `action` (`primary.*`, `secondary.*`).
3. **The component's own recipe** for anything varying by variant/size/state.
4. **`sx`** for a one-off prop-system gap.

Not at the end. **And check the Jira card's Figma link actually points at your frame** — a
stale link propagates: you build the wrong thing, the BA signs off against a different frame,

in a DM.

`uiBuild-knowledge.md` §5.

Roughly 30 minutes stuck is the trigger. One question at a time.

The SOW allows **10 defects, no Sev3** — the whole project, not per sprint. (Contract figure;
nothing in `.docs/` records it.) Expect UI PRs
to be reviewed against the preview environment **and** Figma. Self-review the same way before
you open it (§9) — it's faster than a review round-trip.

## 2. Before you write any code

### Confirm the branch

```bash
git branch --show-current
```

If it's `develop` or `main`, stop. No changes.

### Check what already exists

Read `.claude/registry/` for the component. The `Origin` column is what matters:

| Origin | Means |
|---|---|
| `Custom` | Zimmermann-authored, already here |
| `Override` | already mirrored into `overrides/` |
| **`Base`** | **still upstream — you pay copy-first** |

⚠️ **Do not trust the registry's `Tier` column.** `generateRegistry.mjs:125-203` hardcodes tier
arrays, lists no `ui-kits` path, and defaults everything else to Tier 4. Paths are reliable;
tiers are not. For what actually blocks, read `CODEOWNERS`.

### The three component families

| Family | Casing | Example |
|---|---|---|
| SFCC override | kebab-case, matching upstream exactly | `product-tile/` |
| **ui-kit component** | **camelCase — the default for new work** | `zimmButton/` |
| `shared/ui` primitive | PascalCase, mirroring upstream | `Button/` |

Kebab-case applies *only* to files mirroring a base Salesforce file. Naming a Zimmermann-
authored file in kebab-case falsely signals Salesforce origin — which inverts the convention's
whole purpose.

### Where a new component goes

```
overrides/app/components/ui-kits/{atoms,molecules,organisms}/<camelCase>/
  index.tsx
  index.stories.tsx
  <name>.css.ts          ← the recipe
  index.test.tsx         ← if it has branching or event wiring
```

**Tier by composition, read off the imports:**

- **atom** — imports no other ui-kit
- **molecule** — composes atoms, light local state
- **organism** — composes molecules/atoms **and owns domain state**

An icon passed as a prop doesn't count. Slotted children don't count.

### What's actually overridden today

Eleven directories:

```
_app-config  button  contentful  footer  foundation  header
icons  pageContainer  product-view  ui-kits  uiCopyProvider
```

Still base, despite being referenced throughout `.claude/rules/`: `product-tile`,
`display-price`, `swatch-group`, `image-gallery`, `link`, `list-menu`, `drawer-menu`, `seo`.
**Assume most stories pay copy-first.**

### The copy-first rule

For any task requiring an override that doesn't exist yet, prepare **all of them at once**
before any functional change:

1. Copy each file from `node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/` to the mirrored path.
2. Convert to `.ts`/`.tsx`, update imports.
3. `npx tsc --noEmit`.
4. Add a temporary `console.log('[overrides] product-tile.tsx')` to each.
5. **Stop.** Let the user confirm the overrides are rendering.
6. Remove the `console.log`s, then make functional changes.

Never bundle this silently with functional work.

## 3. Design Foundations

*The longest section, and the part that moves. Read it before your first component.*

### The styling hierarchy

1. **`textStyle`** for anything textual — `textStyle="body2"`, never a raw `fontSize`. All 22
   Handover text styles are registered:

   `heading1Strong` `heading1` `heading2` `heading3` · `body1Strong` `body1` `body2Strong`
   `body2` · `mobileBody1Strong` `mobileBody1` `mobileBody2` · `label` `caption` · `linkLg`
   `linkSm` · `button` `buttonSm` · `productNames` `price` · `navigation` · `footer` · `serif`
2. **`var(--zimm-*)`** for colour and spacing. The spacing scale:

   | | | | | | | |
   |---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
   | `3xs` 2px | `2xs` 4px | `xs` 8px | `s` 12px | `m` 16px | `l` 20px | `xl` 24px |
   | `2xl` 32px | `3xl` 40px | `4xl` 64px | `5xl` 80px | `6xl` 128px | `7xl` 160px | |

   Semantic colour groups in `foundation/colour.ts`: `background` (01–07), `text`, `border`,
   `status`, `link`, `icon`, `action` (`primary.*`, `secondary.*`).
3. **The component's own recipe** for anything varying by variant/size/state.
4. **`sx`** for a one-off prop-system gap.

5. **Scoped `.scss`** only when `sx` genuinely can't express it. In practice: never. There is

### ⚠️ [CORRECTED] Rung 2 inverted — bare token strings are now wrong

An earlier revision of this manual taught `color="text.default"` and `padding="m"`, and said
seeing `var()` in a `.tsx` was a smell. **That is backwards from the current rule.**

```tsx
// ❌ bare Chakra/theme token string in an override component
<Box color="text.default" padding="m" />

// ✅ raw var(--zimm-*) reference
<Box color="var(--zimm-color-text-default)" padding="var(--zimm-scale-m)" />
```

⚠️ **Two different rules are in play and it's easy to conflate them.** A bare key on a *spacing*
prop is **correct but against house style** — `theme.space` is registered, so it resolves. A bare
key on a *sizing or typography* prop is **broken** — those scales aren't registered at all. The
first gets a review comment; the second ships a 576px icon.

The reason is **house style, not correctness** — a bare key resolves identically, but forces a
reviewer to check `theme/index.ts`'s registered-scale list to know whether it's correct.

`textStyle` stays a bare key. It's the one exception: there's no `var()` for the composite.

**In practice this rarely arises**, because brand values mostly shouldn't be in JSX at all.
Measured on `develop`: `var(--zimm-*)` appears in **18 recipe files** and exactly **one**
component `.tsx` — a conditional `paddingLeft` no Chakra prop expresses. Type via `textStyle`,
colour and spacing into the recipe, `var()` in JSX only for a genuine gap.

### Icon, action and motion values are constants, not theme tokens

They collide with Chakra's scales the same way — `theme.sizes.lg` is 32rem and backs `boxSize`
everywhere — so they are **imported directly** rather than registered:

```tsx
import { iconSizes, actionSizes, motion } from 'app/theme/foundation';

<Icon boxSize={iconSizes.lg} />            // 20px
<Button height={actionSizes.height.lg} />  // 52px
```

| | |
|---|---|
| `iconSizes` | `lg` 20px · `md` 16px · `sm` 12px |
| `actionSizes` | `height.{lg: 52, md: 40}` · `paddingX.{lg: 32, md: 20}` · `gap: 16` |
| `motion` | `duration.{fast: 200, default: 300, slow: 500}ms` · `easing.{standard, slides, fades}` |

⚠️ **Motion values are PROVISIONAL**, pending designer sign-off — `motion.ts` says so itself.

`borderWidth.default` is 1px. `focusRingOffsets.default` is 2px, `.secondary` 3px — the second
exists to clear the secondary button's 1px border.

### ⚠️ The trap: a spacing key on a sizing prop

**This shipped a completely broken footer, so it's worth being blunt about.**

```tsx
padding: 'xl',   // ✅ reads theme.space.xl
width: 'xl',     // ❌ reads theme.sizes.xl = 36rem = 576px
```

Only `space` is registered. `sizes`, `fontSizes`, `lineHeights`, `letterSpacings` are not.
Measured blow-up range **8×–112×**. And `s`/`m`/`l` are absent from Chakra's `sizes`, so those
declarations are **dropped silently**.

Nothing catches this. `'xl'` is a valid `SystemStyleObject` value so TypeScript is satisfied,
no lint rule exists, and no test asserts layout. It passed `tsc`, `eslint`, `vitest`,
CodeRabbit (local *and* PR) and the Storybook a11y run — only rendering the page found it.

`recipeGuards.test.ts` now guards it **inside recipes**. It cannot see a JSX prop.

### ⚠️ `extendTheme` MERGES — it does not replace

Name a recipe `Footer` and it deep-merges into base SFCC's `Footer`, inheriting parts you never
wrote. Namespace everything: `ZimmFooter`.

`INTENTIONAL_MERGES = ['Button', 'Header', 'ListMenu']` — those three are deliberate. Anything
else must be namespaced, and `recipeGuards.test.ts` fails the build if it isn't.

⚠️ A recipe unit test **cannot catch this**: `extendTheme` doesn't populate `theme.__cssMap`,
only `ChakraProvider` does. A direct `css()(theme)` assertion passes vacuously.

### Responsive steps are explicit media queries

```ts
[`@media (min-width: ${BP.tablet})`]: {
  flexDirection: 'row',
  padding: `var(--zimm-scale-4xl) var(--zimm-scale-3xl) ${SPACE_SECTION}`,
},
```

Two reasons. The array shorthand (`['2xs','2xs','xs','xs']`) puts a bare token key at every
step and the guard flags all four. And `BP.desktop` (64em) **conflicts with Chakra's `lg`=62em
/ `xl`=80em**, so a responsive prop silently steps at the wrong width.

### Register the recipe or it throws

Chakra resolves a recipe by the string key passed to `useMultiStyleConfig`, not by file path.
Co-location is therefore free — but the key must be in `theme/components/index.ts` or
destructuring throws at runtime.

**A registered recipe nothing reads is dead code.** Chakra's `<Button>`/`<Link>` read theirs
automatically; a custom multipart component must call `useMultiStyleConfig` (or `useStyleConfig`
for a single-part one). A registered-but-unread recipe looks like compliance and changes nothing.

The consumption pattern is always three lines:

```ts
const ZIMM_FOOTER_RECIPE = 'ZimmFooter';
const styles = useMultiStyleConfig(ZIMM_FOOTER_RECIPE, {});
```

### Interaction state belongs in CSS, not React state

`_hover`, `_active`, `_focusVisible`, `_disabled` in the recipe. Not `useState` + `onMouseEnter`.
It looks identical in a screenshot and behaves differently in five ways that all matter:
touch devices, keyboard focus, rapid pointer movement, SSR output, and re-render cost.

⚠️ A programmatic `.focus()` does **not** match `:focus-visible`. A ring styled only on
`:focus-visible` won't appear after a scripted focus move.

### `.zimm-*` global classes

~28 classes live in `globalStyles.ts` — `.zimm-text-*`, `.zimm-form-*`, `.zimm-grid`,
`.zimm-focus-visible`. They ship on **every page** and have almost no consumers today (one
Storybook demo uses `.zimm-grid`).

**There are no `.zimm-btn-*` classes, and there must never be.** A component with both a class
and a recipe has two surfaces that drift. Use Chakra's `<Button>`.

Don't reach for a class for new work — a registered recipe, always. The classes remain
defensible only for genuinely static, non-interactive, massively-reused treatments.

### You don't add tokens

A missing token is an escalation to the UI designer (§8), not a number you invent.

If you must ship a placeholder pending sign-off, make it a **named constant with a comment
containing `provisional`, `pending`, or `placeholder`** — `npm run audit:tokens` reads that
comment and downgrades the finding to an acknowledged exception rather than a violation.
`audit-allow: <reason>` works too.

Current state: **19 unacknowledged violations** repo-wide. Don't add to it.

### Compound values and shorthand order

```ts
padding: 'xs 0',        // ❌ emitted verbatim, browser drops it
paddingInline: 0,       // ✅
```

Chakra resolves a token only as the **entire** value. And a shorthand declared *after* a
longhand resets it — `padding: 0` after `paddingBlock` wipes it.

### Figma comparison

Text nodes report a **cap-height box** and are **not comparable** to a CSS line box. Frames and
instances report a **real box** and are. A uniform residual across siblings is measurement; a
varying one is a defect. Full method in `uiBuild-knowledge.md` §5.

### Step 1 — does it exist?

Registry, then `ui-kits/`, then the base package.

### Step 2 — pick the rung

**Use as-is** → done.

**Override** → copy-first (§2). Keep the kebab-case filename. If the component is used
internally by SFCC's own components, the **default export must stay a faithful port** — full
prop surface, same `forwardRef` — with Zimmermann styling behind a named export. Check with:

```bash

```

(`'../swatch-group'`), not the base path. The resolver is webpack-only — Storybook and Vitest
don't load it, so a base-path import silently renders the **unstyled base component** in both.

**Build custom** → §2's folder layout.

### Step 3 — execute

Named export matching the folder. Props type named for the component, declared at the top of
the file. Move it to `types.ts` only when a sibling file consumes it.

**Split when:** the component function passes ~150 lines, or branching gets deep. **Extract to
a hook when:** there are ≥2 related `useState` that change together, or a `useEffect` has a
non-trivial dependency array or a cleanup function.

### Step 4 — apply design styles

Recipe first. `sx` for genuine gaps. Never a raw literal.

Every file has a `Default`. Add named exports for meaningful states (`Loading`, `OutOfStock`),
not every prop combination. Add `play` only where there's interactive behaviour worth
asserting.

```tsx
import {expect, userEvent, within} from 'storybook/test'
```

⚠️ **`@storybook/test` is not installed.** `.claude/rules/testing.md:115` prescribes it;
Storybook 10 moved it to `storybook/test`. Following that line verbatim breaks. The rule is
wrong, not your code.

### Two things Storybook won't show truthfully

- **Base-template SVGs render as empty boxes.** `.storybook/main.js` `ignore-loader`s them,
  mirroring the browser build — so an icon sourced from `@salesforce/retail-react-app` shows
  blank in Storybook while rendering correctly in the app. Our own icons in `zimm.tsx` are
  unaffected. **A blank icon in Storybook is usually a sourcing signal, not a broken glyph.**
- **`test-storybook` needs a *built* Storybook.** Running it against the dev server makes
  results uninterpretable.
- **Portalled content is not inside `canvasElement`.** `canvasElement` is `#storybook-root`, a
  *sibling* of the portal target. Measured: 0 dialogs inside the canvas against 1 in the
  document. Query `document` for a portalled dialog and use `findByRole`, not `getByRole` —
  the render promise resolves from `useLayoutEffect`, before passive effects have mounted the
  portal. `testing.md:128`'s "never reach into `document`" has no portal carve-out; that's a
  documentation gap.

### The commands

```bash
npm run storybook                                # the build surface
npm run build-storybook && npx test-storybook    # interaction + a11y — needs a BUILT storybook
```

Interaction tests catch things the other layers can't: on the footer PR, making a text-input
control opt-in removed a button a `play` function clicked. `tsc`, `lint` and `vitest` were all
green; CI caught it at **1 failure in 73**.

### Your branch gets a live MRT URL automatically

`deploy-preview.yml` deploys every push to `feature/**`/`fix/**` to its own ephemeral MRT
environment and posts the URL. Use it for the three-surface review in §9.

- **One environment per branch, not per commit** — reused on later pushes, and the comment
  updates in place.
- **Torn down automatically** when the PR closes or the branch is deleted.
- A real Sydney-hosted (`ap-southeast-2`) storefront with real dev environment variables — not

**Your component is not done until its data exists where it ships.**

This is new, and it's here because the footer passed every gate, rendered perfectly in dev and

### The two mechanisms are separate

|---|---|---|
| Deploy | `npm run install:contentful -- --target <env>` | *nothing automated* |

**An Environment Template cannot carry entries.** It's structural — the SDK type has slots for

| tier | types | entries |
|---|---|---|
| **dev** | 14 | 42 |
| test / sit / uat / staging | **0** | **0** |

template covers only 5 of dev's 14 types** — the other 9 were UI-authored and have no code
representation.

### Before you say a component works on a tier

```bash
curl -s "https://cdn.contentful.com/spaces/<space>/environments/<env>/entries?content_type=<type>&limit=1" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <that tier's delivery token>"
```

`total: 1` → it will render. `unknownContentType` → the model was never installed. Use
`limit=1`; the CDA returns an unreliable `total` at `limit=0`.

### Fetch depth is load-bearing

The footer passes `include: 3` (`footer/index.tsx:27`) where the shared `useContentful.ts`
hardcodes `include=2`. That is not arbitrary. At depth 2 the `regions` array arrives as unresolved stubs, a
field access throws, the `.catch` swallows it, and the **entire component renders nothing**.

### Two things Storybook won't show truthfully

- **Base-template SVGs render as empty boxes.** `.storybook/main.js` `ignore-loader`s them,

  results uninterpretable.
- **Portalled content is not inside `canvasElement`.** `canvasElement` is `#storybook-root`, a
  *sibling* of the portal target. Measured: 0 dialogs inside the canvas against 1 in the
  document. Query `document` for a portalled dialog and use `findByRole`, not `getByRole` —
  the render promise resolves from `useLayoutEffect`, before passive effects have mounted the
  portal. `testing.md:128`'s "never reach into `document`" has no portal carve-out; that's a
  documentation gap.

## 10. Responding to a CodeRabbit review

**Reply in-thread to every finding — fixed or not.** CodeRabbit's learning picks up patterns
from PR conversation. Silence teaches it nothing; a fix commit with no reply doesn't count.

- **Fixed** → a short reply confirming it, referencing the commit.
- **Not fixing** → explain *which specific rule or doc* justifies it, so the same pattern gets
  recognised next time instead of re-flagged.

Nothing enforces this: `requiresConversationResolution` is `false` on all three protected
branches, so a PR merges with every thread unanswered.

### What the declines on PR #59 established

These encode more project convention than the fixes did:

- **Only four files are true absolutes** — `ssr.js`, `config/default.js`, `config/sites.js`,
  `worker/main.js`. Being Tier 1 is not by itself disqualifying; being one of the four named
  absolutes is.
- **Never argue "the rationale isn't engaged"** against unconditionally-worded text. That's an
  over-read, and it was conceded as one.
- **An incidental Tier 1 edit that *could* be split out *should* be.** Declining on mootness is
  the weak position.
- **Fixing a bug in one component doesn't license touching its neighbours** (Hard Rule #5) —
  even a confirmed real bug, if it's pre-existing and out of scope. The systemic fix is a lint
  rule with its own story.
- **Never accept CodeRabbit's offer to open a GitHub issue.** This project tracks in Jira; a
  GitHub issue is a parallel tracker nobody watches.
- **When a repo rule is stated unconditionally, conform even for a provable no-op** — and add
  an inline comment saying so, so the next reader doesn't hunt for phantom state.
- **Cite the PRD line before you cite it.** A wrong citation in a decline poisons CodeRabbit's
  learning store and has to be retracted in-thread, not silently amended in a later commit.

### Two switches that silence it invisibly

`chore(deps)` or `dependabot` **in the PR title** disables CodeRabbit entirely — title-matched,
not author-matched. So does draft status. Neither shows as a failing check; it just goes quiet.

## 11. Hard stops

1. Never work on `develop` or `main`.
2. Never modify a Tier 1 file without it being named in the prompt and owner approval confirmed.
3. Never modify `overrides/app/theme/foundation/`.
4. Never modify `ssr.js`, `config/default.js`, `config/sites.js`, `worker/main.js` — absolute,
   no exception.
5. Never refactor upward. Fixing a component doesn't mean touching the hook it calls.
6. Never rename or move a shared hook or component.
7. Never add or remove packages without Integration approval. When approved, `npm install` —
   don't hand-edit `package.json`.
8. Never modify test configuration.
9. Never delete files without being explicitly asked.
10. Never touch more than one protection tier in a change without confirming scope.
11. Never commit, push, or open a PR without an explicit request in the current prompt.
    Resuming from a summary or a "natural next step" is not an instruction to commit.

### Shared shell needs coordination

`header/`, `footer/`, `drawer-menu/`, `list-menu/`, `seo/`, `_app/`, `_app-config/`,
`uiCopyProvider/`, `routes.tsx` are Tier 2 Global Shell, owned by **both** squads. Coordinate
before touching.

⚠️ **`.claude/rules/` is documentation; `CODEOWNERS` is configuration.** When you want to know
what will actually block a merge, read `CODEOWNERS`. It has **no catch-all rule**, so a path
absent from it needs no code-owner review regardless of what any rules file says. `squadA.md`
and `squadB.md` are six weeks stale and contradict `CODEOWNERS` on PDP ownership — CODEOWNERS
says Squad B and is the one that enforces.

## 12. Performance

LCP ≤ **2s at p75 mobile**. Not a polish pass.

- **Images** — always lazy-load, always serve correctly sized. Never render a full-resolution
  image at thumbnail size.
- **Code splitting** — dynamic `import()` for anything heavy not needed on first render.
- **Data fetching** — request only the fields you need; parallelise. Waterfalls are not
  acceptable.
- **Third-party** — nothing loads before consent, and nothing consent-gated may block LCP. Use
  `defer`, `async`, or post-hydration injection.
- **Bundle** — `main.js` ≤ 180 kB, `vendor.js` ≤ 550 kB, enforced by `bundlesize2`.

⚠️ **No CSS budget exists.** `projectState.md`'s "main.css < 50 kB" was never implemented. CSS
growth is currently ungated in both directions.

### The eight things people get wrong most

1. A bare token key on a **sizing** prop — `width: 'xl'` = 576px.
2. A recipe not namespaced, silently merging into a base SFCC recipe.
3. A recipe not registered — runtime throw on destructuring.
4. A base-path import of an already-overridden component — renders the base version in
   Storybook and Vitest.
5. `padding: 'xs 0'` — compound values never tokenise.
6. A raw literal with no `provisional`/`pending` comment.
7. Assuming the component is broken when the **data doesn't exist on that tier**.
8. Reading a PR's head-SHA checks as green when they're actually `skipping`.

2. Never modify a Tier 1 file without it being named in the prompt and owner approval confirmed.
3. Never modify `overrides/app/theme/foundation/`.
4. Never modify `ssr.js`, `config/default.js`, `config/sites.js`, `worker/main.js` — absolute,
   no exception.
5. Never refactor upward. Fixing a component doesn't mean touching the hook it calls.
6. Never rename or move a shared hook or component.
7. Never add or remove packages without Integration approval. When approved, `npm install` —
   don't hand-edit `package.json`.
8. Never modify test configuration.
9. Never delete files without being explicitly asked.
10. Never touch more than one protection tier in a change without confirming scope.
11. Never commit, push, or open a PR without an explicit request in the current prompt.
    Resuming from a summary or a "natural next step" is not an instruction to commit.

### Shared shell needs coordination

`header/`, `footer/`, `drawer-menu/`, `list-menu/`, `seo/`, `_app/`, `_app-config/`,
`uiCopyProvider/`, `routes.tsx` are Tier 2 Global Shell, owned by **both** squads. Coordinate
before touching.

⚠️ **`.claude/rules/` is documentation; `CODEOWNERS` is configuration.** When you want to know
what will actually block a merge, read `CODEOWNERS`. It has **no catch-all rule**, so a path
absent from it needs no code-owner review regardless of what any rules file says. `squadA.md`
and `squadB.md` are six weeks stale and contradict `CODEOWNERS` on PDP ownership — CODEOWNERS
says Squad B and is the one that enforces.

---

## 12. Performance

LCP ≤ **2s at p75 mobile**. Not a polish pass.

- **Images** — always lazy-load, always serve correctly sized. Never render a full-resolution
  image at thumbnail size.
- **Code splitting** — dynamic `import()` for anything heavy not needed on first render.
- **Data fetching** — request only the fields you need; parallelise. Waterfalls are not
  acceptable.
- **Third-party** — nothing loads before consent, and nothing consent-gated may block LCP. Use
  `defer`, `async`, or post-hydration injection.
- **Bundle** — `main.js` ≤ 180 kB, `vendor.js` ≤ 550 kB, enforced by `bundlesize2`.

⚠️ **No CSS budget exists.** `projectState.md`'s "main.css < 50 kB" was never implemented. CSS
growth is currently ungated in both directions.

---

## 13. Quick reference

```bash
/session-start                   # branch check + tracking docs + health check
/scope-check                     # is this in this sprint, and whose territory?
/code-quality                    # read-only audit of the branch diff
/pr-checklist                    # pre-PR sweep
```

```bash
npx tsc --noEmit                 # gated nowhere — run it yourself
npm run lint                     # gated nowhere
npm run test                     # Vitest — required check on develop
npm run audit:tokens             # gated nowhere; 19 violations outstanding
npm run build
cr review --light --base develop
```

`npm start` — **do not run.** Ask for a restart if needed.

| What | Where |
|---|---|
| Design tokens (Tier 1) | `overrides/app/theme/foundation/` |
| Registered recipes | `overrides/app/theme/components/index.ts` |
| Co-located recipe | `<component>/<name>.css.ts` |
| Zimmermann components | `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/{atoms,molecules,organisms}/` |
| Icons — **single source of truth** | `overrides/app/components/icons` |
| Shared types | `overrides/app/types/` |

**Icons:** never import from `@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/icons`. If an icon is
missing from the overrides set, ask — don't substitute a visually similar one.
(`header/index.tsx:60` currently violates this.)

### The eight things people get wrong most

1. A bare token key on a **sizing** prop — `width: 'xl'` = 576px.
2. A recipe not namespaced, silently merging into a base SFCC recipe.
3. A recipe not registered — runtime throw on destructuring.
4. A base-path import of an already-overridden component — renders the base version in
   Storybook and Vitest.
5. `padding: 'xs 0'` — compound values never tokenise.
6. A raw literal with no `provisional`/`pending` comment.
7. Assuming the component is broken when the **data doesn't exist on that tier**.
8. Reading a PR's head-SHA checks as green when they're actually `skipping`.

---

per tier) and section 10 (responding to CodeRabbit) are new.*

That route cannot express this requirement: a wrapper can only set props the default already accepts, so letting a caller replace an internal render block still requires the slot on the default. The only alternative is forking the component body, which is a graver breach of the faithful-port rule. The rule's stated purpose is served. renderHeader has zero occurrences in the base package, and the four base modules that import product-view — product-view-modal/index.jsx, product-view-modal/bundle.jsx, bonus-product-view-modal/index.jsx and pages/product-detail/index.jsx — neither pass it nor are affected by it. forwardRef behaviour is unchanged. Note overrideStyling.md cites product-tile/index.tsx (CardBaseline) and link/index.tsx as established precedent for the named-export split. Neither exists in overrides/, and CardBaseline appears nowhere in the codebase. Raised separately. ProductViewRefScope's JSDoc told consumers to assert Ref at the prop site. That is not required — TypeScript accepts the this-typed callback as a ref unaided, verified by removing the equivalent assertion and observing a clean typecheck against a live probe. The guidance sat in a shared component, so it propagated. It is now descriptive. Three inert casts removed -------------------------- The cloneElement trio narrowed nothing: customButton.props is any, since React.ReactElement defaults P = any, and Partial is {}. typescript.md reserves `as` for genuinely overriding inference, so documenting them would not have cured them. # Special Components

:::note
This guide assumes that you’re familiar with how routing works in a PWA Kit storefront. To learn more, see our guide to [Routing](/docs/commerce/b2c-commerce/guide/routing.md).
:::

The PWA Kit React SDK includes the following special components: `AppConfig`, `App`, `Error`, and `Document`.

The default implementation of each special component can be overridden by your own custom version so that you can configure and customize the behavior of your storefront across multiple pages.

Let’s look at each special component separately:

## AppConfig

The `AppConfig` component is positioned near the top of the component hierarchy in your React app. From this position, it allows you to insert code to configure and support app-wide features, such as [state management](/docs/commerce/b2c-commerce/guide/managing-global-state.md) or component theming. In the Retail React App, the `ChakraProvider` component is inserted into `AppConfig` to make theme values (for colors, spacing, and so on) available to all the [Chakra UI](https://chakra-ui.com/) components.

The `AppConfig` component also lets you extend the set of arguments that get passed to all components that are enhanced by `routeComponent` via the `getProps` function. To add these arguments, define a function called `extraGetPropsArgs` as a property of the `AppConfig` component.

The Retail React App uses the `extraGetPropsArgs` function to give all components that are enhanced by `routeComponent` access to an object for interacting with the Salesforce Commerce API:

```javascript
AppConfig.restore = (locals = {}) => {
  locals.api = new CommerceAPI(apiConfig)
}

AppConfig.freeze = () => undefined

AppConfig.extraGetPropsArgs = (locals = {}) => {
  return {
    api: locals.api
  }
}
```

The version of the `AppConfig` component from the PWA Kit React SDK doesn’t do much—unless you override it. To override the SDK version of `AppConfig`, define a file in `app/components/_app-config/index.jsx`. A newly generated PWA Kit project already includes this file to get you started.

## App

The `App` component is a child of the `AppConfig` component. Its main purpose is to include any components for layout and UI that persist throughout your React app, such as the header, footer, and sidebar.

The `App` component is also enhanced by the `routeComponent` function. If you define a `getProps` function as a property of the `App` component, it gets called when *any* component from the `routes` array is rendered. Use it for any logic that you’d like to run on every page.

Like `AppConfig`, a default version of the `App` component exists in the PWA Kit React SDK, and you’re encouraged to override it. To override the SDK version of `App`, define a file in `app/components/_app/index.jsx`. A newly generated PWA Kit project already includes this file to get you started.

Some of the features that are implemented in `App` for a newly generated project include: analytics tracking, offline detection, and the `SkipNavLink` component for accessibility.

## Error

The `Error` component is rendered in place of the `App` component under any of the following conditions:

- The user makes a request for a path that isn’t found in the `routes` array.
- A component from the `routes` array throws an error in its `getProps` function.
- A component from the `routes` array throws an error during rendering.

When the `Error` component is returned, an HTTP 404 status is also included in the response header.

Like the other special components, the PWA Kit React SDK includes a default version of the `Error` component, and you’re encouraged to override it. To override the SDK version of `Error`, define a file in `app/components/_error/index.jsx`. A newly generated PWA Kit project already includes this file to get you started.

By overriding the `Error` component, you can do things like customize the error page for your brand, add redirects, and track the error as an analytics event.

## Document

The `Document` component defines the HTML that surrounds your application, such as the `<html>`, `<head>`, and `<body>` tags.

Like the other special components, the PWA Kit React SDK includes a default version of the `Document` component that can be overridden. But, in this case, we *don’t* recommend that you override it. But if you need fine-grained control over your application, you can override `Document` by defining a file in `app/components/_document/index.jsx`. A newly generated PWA Kit project does *not* include this file.

:::tip
Rather than override the `Document` component, we recommend using the [React Helmet](https://www.npmjs.com/package/react-helmet) library to modify the HTML tags in `Document`, such as `<head>`.
:::
=====WORKFLOWS=====
# Development Workflow Differences with PWA Kit

PWA Kit uses a traditional Webpack-based development server with configuration spread across multiple files. Storefront Next leverages Vite for faster development with native ESM, instant HMR, and type-safe configuration. The shift to Vite provides a more modern developer experience with faster feedback loops and better tooling integration.

## Key Differences

| Aspect        | PWA Kit             | Storefront Next              |
| ------------- | ------------------- | ---------------------------- |
| Dev Server    | Webpack Dev Server  | Vite Dev Server              |
| CLI Tool      | `pwa-kit-dev start` | `sfnext dev`                 |
| HMR           | Webpack HMR         | Vite native HMR              |
| Config Format | JavaScript          | TypeScript                   |
| Env Vars      | Standard .env       | Typed with `PUBLIC__` prefix |
| Testing       | Jest                | Vitest                       |
| Type Safety   | Optional            | Required                     |

## Key Similarities

1. Port conventions: Both can run on any port.
2. API proxy pattern: Both use `/mobify/proxy/` path.
3. Environment variables: Both support .env files.
4. Node.js debugging: Both support `--inspect` flag.
5. Express-based: Both use Express for SSR.

## Storefront Conversion Considerations

1. Port Change

   - Update any hardcoded port references from 3000 to 5173.
   - Or configure Vite to use port 3000.

2. Environment Variables

   - Convert standard env vars to `PUBLIC__` prefix format.
   - Update .env files with new naming convention.

3. Config Migration

   - Convert `config/default.js` to `config.server.ts`.
   - Add TypeScript types for configuration.

4. Testing Migration
   - Convert Jest tests to Vitest.
   - Update test configuration files.

### The product-side register — live, decision-blocking

| Open item | Position to hold |
|---|---|
| **Recommendations** | `SFCC-7` already holds eight decomposed tickets, and **SFCC-647 is `Ready for Development`** and answers the data-source question. Raise 647 — don't create tickets. |
| **Shop the Look naming** | Four names for possibly two things: "Shop the Look" (SFCC-90), "Shop the Edit" (SFCC-313), "Product Cards with Lookbook" (04.7), and `shoppableImage`, which already exists in code. Force one name before either is estimated. |
| **Preview & publishing** | The preview token is set on dev/test/sit/uat only — never staging/prod. Both preview paths 404 without it and are `noindex`. **Authors preview on `uat`.** "Can we preview on prod?" needs a Tier 1 change against a documented security rationale. |
| **Contentful pattern per component** | Entry-driven vs Studio Experiences. **Highest-value item to close** — it decides story order and whether the incremental-assembly loop is even available. |
| **`regions` content-model field** | Unconfirmed, and it affects every Contentful component's variant model across eight storefronts. |
| **Composed-page ownership** | "Not product/category → Contentful" doesn't settle PDP/PLP editorial blocks or category landing pages. **Category landing pages are the sharp edge, and PLP work is already in flight.** |

---

## Play 9 — Design-system escalation

Standing route for missing tokens: the weekly design review.

Live gaps:

- **Button has no Colour axis.** The 04.7 spec says "Normal, Inverse"; the implementation
  exposes only `variant` + `size`. The registry reports **10 consumers**, so adding the axis
  later touches ten call sites.
- **Icon Button is marked Done in 04.7 and has no implementation at all.**
- `zimmButton`'s provisional heights (50px/41px) disagree with Handover's `actionSizes`
  (52px/40px); `BTN_PADDING_Y` (5px) has no token at all.
- **`textStyles.navigation`** is the only one of 22 hardcoding `lineHeight: 'normal'`; Figma
  reportedly specifies 100%.
- **Spacing gaps** — 28px and 44px are in use with no named entry between `xl` (24) and `2xl`
  (32), or `3xl` (40) and `4xl` (64).
- Primary-button hover fails AA at **2.96:1**; there's no inverse focus-ring token.

⚠️ **"Done" in the 04.7 component tracker means design-confirmed, not API-matched.** Those are
different states and the tracker doesn't distinguish them.

**What to do when the design system itself is wrong** — e.g. a token that fails the project's
own WCAG 2.2 AA target — is unresolved. Someone has to accept that risk explicitly; right now
nobody has.

---

## Governance — what actually blocks

*Expanded. The short version: `.claude/rules/` is documentation, `CODEOWNERS` is
configuration.*

### The real enforcement

Server-side and it works: `require_code_owner_reviews` + `enforce_admins` +
`bypass_pull_request_allowances: []` on `develop`, `main` and `release/**`. All five CODEOWNERS
teams exist and have members.

Advisory only: `tier1-guard`, `tier2-warning`, `cross-squad-guard`, and any assistant's
confirmation prompt. `tier1-guard` is deliberately not a required check — GitHub's Feb-2025
cross-run check-run lockdown made "hard-fail until approved" unimplementable.

### Where the docs and the configuration disagree

| Path | Declared | CODEOWNERS | CI guard |
|---|---|---|---|
| `babel.config.js` | **Tier 1** | **absent** | **absent** |
| `tsconfig.json` | **Tier 1** | **absent** | **absent** |
| `theme/globalStyles.ts` | **Tier 2** | **absent** | **absent** |
| `overrides/app/ssr/**` | Tier 1 | ✓ | absent — the glob is `ssr.*`, a literal dot |

**`CODEOWNERS` has no catch-all rule.** A path absent from it requires zero code-owner review
regardless of what any rules file says. So editing `tsconfig.json` — strict mode and every path
alias — currently needs approval from nobody.

Also ungated: `scripts/versionGuard.mjs` (the entire downgrade-protection mechanism),
`.husky/*` (the shims that invoke the gated hooks — empty one and the gate is off).

### Last-match-wins

`CODEOWNERS:186` (`overrides/app/components/**/*.css.ts` → squads only) is placed last among
the `components/` rules, deliberately downgrading any co-located recipe inside a Tier 2
directory. Rationale: a co-located recipe composes established tokens; authoring a new token
still means `theme/foundation/`.

⚠️ It also means a `.css.ts` inside `_app-config/` or `seo/` would drop the Tier 2 gate the
same way. Nothing prevents that.

### Squad ownership is stale

`squadA.md` and `squadB.md` were last touched 2026-07-14 — six weeks behind the actively
maintained rules files, though `conventions.md` and `typescript.md` are nominally older still. Of squadA's 21
territory paths, 4 exist; **zero** of squadB's 9 do. Both contradict `CODEOWNERS` on PDP
ownership — **CODEOWNERS says Squad B and is the one that enforces.**

### Tier 1 approval

Four files are absolute: `ssr.js`, `config/default.js`, `config/sites.js`, `worker/main.js`.
Everything else Tier 1 is reachable under the verified-session exception — `gh api user`, check
`tier-1-approvers` membership, then name the file and the reason **in the commit body**.

Being Tier 1 is not by itself disqualifying; being one of the four named absolutes is.

⚠️ **`tier-2-approvers` has 2 members and `tier-1-approvers` has 3.** Any PR touching
`theme/components/` is a two-person bus factor.

---

input.description: Read fedLead-playbook opening

content.content:
# FED Lead Playbook

**Owner:** Marcel Navarro · **Started:** August 2026 · **Revised:** 25 August 2026

The lead role: what you say, to whom, and when. Judgement and process, not procedure.

**Companions:** `fedBuild-manual.md` (how to build a component) · `uiBuild-knowledge.md` (why
the machine behaves the way it does).

**Authority on styling:** `.claude/rules/overrideStyling.md`. If this file disagrees with it,
that file wins.

*This document absorbed `zimmermann_frontend_lead_playbook.md` (retired 25 Aug 2026). Its
durable operating principles are §3; its training-vehicle material — a Next.js/Tailwind stack
that isn't this one — was dropped.*

---

## 1. The mandate

Sixteen responsibilities landed across two Contentful-vs-PWA-Kit alignment meetings. They
reduce to two mandates:

- **M1 — Protect the build.** Reuse, conventions, review, accessibility, performance.
- **M2 — Protect the plan.** Estimation, scope, dependencies, escalation.

**The one to resist as stated:** being a serial refinement gate across both squads. It won't
scale and it will slip. Name that rather than absorbing it — an unresourced ask that quietly
becomes yours is the failure mode here.

### The quality bar this serves

The SOW allows **10 defects, no Sev3**, for the whole project. (Contract figure — nothing in
`.docs/` records it, so cite the SOW itself, not the repo.) Three consequences:

1. **Vigilance is the job**, not an overhead on it.
2. **Budget real time per UI PR** — an hour or more. That's the cost of the review, not
   slippage.
3. **Flag rather than invent.** A guessed value that ships is a defect with your name on it.

---

## 2. Operating rhythm

| Moment | Plays |
|---|---|
| Story drafting | 1, 3, 4 |

content.content:
### Polishing is procrastination

If an edit to a rules file didn't change what someone can or can't do, it wasn't a real edit.

### Define done, or nothing stops

This applies to people and tools equally. "Improve the footer" has no terminal state.

---

## 4. Working with AI tooling

*New section. The expensive failures on this project were not bad code — they were unrequested
work and unrequested commits.*

### The authorisation ladder — three separate levels

**Investigate ≠ fix ≠ commit.** "Run it" and "have a look" are investigation requests. They are
not approval to change code, and changing code is not approval to commit it.

Correct shape: **change → verify → stop and show the diff → wait.**

This sharpens AGENTS.md Hard Rule #15 with the distinction the rule leaves implicit. Resuming
from a session summary, a task list, or a "natural next step" is **not** an instruction to
commit.

### The audit-loop failure mode

A build can become a self-sustaining audit-and-fix cycle that feels productive and isn't.
Measured on one stretch of SFCC-55: **55 commits, a 3.0:1 rework ratio, `footer/index.tsx`
touched 32 times in 5 days.** The work wasn't wasted — it was mis-ordered.

**The diagnostic that separates real work from generated work:** where did the finding come
from? Six findings fixed things that were actually broken. Seven came from *reading code we'd
just written*. If a finding's origin is your own fresh output rather than a spec, a reproduced
failure, or a review comment, it is probably not the next thing to do.

Two correctives:

- **Read the review queue before starting a self-directed pass.** A six-hour-old Major finding
  named a live security bypass while the loop was polishing comment placement.
- **Ban "it's good practice" as a justification.** A fix needs a named requirement, a
  reproduced failure, or a review comment behind it.

### Present verdicts, don't auto-fix

When a pass produces a list of possible improvements, separate the ones traceable to a
spec/failure/review from the ones traceable to your own just-written code — and **offer** the
second group rather than doing them.

### Don't take an agent's report at face value

Two agent claims were overturned by direct verification in a single session this week: that
a11y is ungated (it is gated — the agent was reasoning from Storybook 8), and that the CLI
would work with the repo's management token (it reads neither that env var nor any other).

Both were confidently stated and internally coherent. **The check is cheap; the propagation
cost is not** — a wrong claim in a doc gets cited for months.

### Local-only docs stay local

These three files live on this machine. **Never cite them in a PR reply, a commit message, or
a code comment.** A citation nobody else can open reads as an appeal to a private authority,
and for CodeRabbit specifically it teaches the bot nothing.

When a local doc is the real reason for a decision, find the public equivalent in `AGENTS.md`,
`.claude/rules/` or `.docs/` and cite that. If none exists, argue the merits directly.

No `Co-Authored-By` trailer on commits.

---

### Shipping discipline

Fixed-price clock, 10-defect budget. Four rules that follow from that:

- **Deploy first.** A thing that runs somewhere other than your machine is the only evidence
  that counts.
- **Partial-but-hardened beats complete-but-broken.** Three states done properly ships; six
  states half-wired doesn't.
- **Descope, never cut quality.** Cutting the loading state to hit a date converts a schedule
  problem into a defect-budget problem, and the budget is smaller.
- **The 20-minute rule.** Twenty minutes without progress is a signal to change approach or
  ask, not to push harder.

### Three states are AC, not polish

Every component that renders fetched data needs **loading** (a skeleton, not a spinner),
**error** (with retry), and **absent** (see `uiBuild-knowledge.md` §7) specified in the story.
If they aren't in the AC they won't be built, and they're where the defects come from.

Related tell: an **invented data source** is a story problem, not a code problem — fix the
story. And an over-engineering tell worth naming: a component estimated at 25–35 lines coming
back as 120.

### Review culture

The PR mechanics are §Play 5. The culture is this:

- **Regroup every work block**, not just at sprint boundaries.
- **Learn from the work, don't judge the person.** A review that makes someone defensive costs
  more than the defect it found.
- **Rotate who's on screen.** The person driving learns most; it shouldn't always be you.
- **The showcase is honest, not polished.** Demo the real state.
- **Commitments are specific enough to check.** "I'll look at it" isn't one.

### The corrections-to-rules loop

**The highest-leverage question you can ask at the end of a work block:** *where did the tooling
make a decision I didn't specify — and what would I add to the AC or the rules to prevent that
next time?*

A correction you make once and forget is a correction you'll make fifty times. And test each
candidate rule against: **is this something that can be checked against, or an aspiration that
will be ignored?**

Second question, equally cheap: **"is that gap fixed now, or did you just acknowledge it?"**
Acknowledgement reads like resolution and isn't.

content.content: ## Play 5 — PR review ### Already mechanical — don't spend review time here Conventional commit format · registry regeneration · derived-config edit blocking · `.env.sample` secret shapes · tag naming · the two `semgrep.yml` security rules (unsanitised `dangerouslySetInnerHTML`, payment-credential logging) · the three ast-grep a11y rules (`warning` only) · Storybook a11y (`preview.tsx` sets `a11y.test: 'error'`; the installed test-runner enforces it). ⚠️ By Play 5b's own standard the a11y gate is **unproven** — it has never been made to fail on purpose. It's on this list because it runs, not because it's been demonstrated to catch anything. Worth one deliberate break to find out. ### Gate zero — does it build ⚠️ **Read the check *history*, not the head SHA.** `detect-changes` diffs `since_last_remote_commit`, so a docs-only final commit flips both required checks green even if an earlier push failed them. **A skipped required check counts as passing.** PR #59 merged with all four suites `skipping` and zero test evidence on its head SHA. Also: `Playwright E2E (localhost)` and `Cross-browser E2E (BrowserStack)` are **required nowhere** — they can be red and the PR merges. ### Review across three surfaces 1. **The diff** — tokens, naming, dead code, test coverage. 2. **The preview environment** — every `feature/**`/`fix/**` push (except `fix/release-*`) gets its own MRT URL. 3. **Figma, side by side**, mobile *and* desktop. Layout defects are invisible in a diff and invisible to every automated gate. `width: 'xl'` resolving to 576px destroyed the footer on every page while passing `tsc`, `eslint`, `vitest`, CodeRabbit twice, and the a11y run. ### The token checklist - Bare token key on a **sizing** or **typography** prop → wrong or dropped silently - Bare token string where `var(--zimm-*)` is now required - Raw hex/px/rem/em without a `provisional`/`pending`/`audit-allow` comment - Recipe not namespaced → silent deep-merge into a base SFCC recipe - Recipe not registered → runtime throw - Compound value (`padding: 'xs 0'`) → emitted verbatim, dropped ### Tests and stories — the minimum A story for anything exported. A test where there's branching or event wiring. Resolve duplicate coverage by **scoping what the test asserts** — mock the child whose internals are proven elsewhere — not by leaving the component with no test of its own. ### Ten questions, in order 1. Does it build, and did the checks actually *run*? 2. Does it match Figma at both breakpoints? 3. Is anything here already in `ui-kits`? 4. Any raw design value? 5. Any bare token key on a sizing/typography prop? 6. Is the recipe namespaced and registered? 7. Keyboard operable, focus visible, names on controls, 24×24 targets? 8. Does the absent-data case render something perceivable? 9. Does its data exist on the tiers it must demo on? 10. Does the protection-tier block in the PR body match the actual diff? --- ## Play 5b — Verifying a claim before you act on it *Learned expensively. Reversals here would each have shipped a wrong change.* - **Absence in an extracted spec is not a decision.** A field missing from a Figma export may mean "not specified" or "deliberately none" — those are different, and you can't tell from the absence. - **A codebase value isn't a spec until you find its source.** Someone typed it. Find out who and why before treating it as intent. - **Ask for the node.** A Figma *screenshot* in a ticket is not the frame. Node type decides whether a measurement is even comparable. - **Value-matching audits produce confident nonsense.** "These 41 literals should be tokens" inflated from 19 by matching `.rem` inside `removeEventListener`. - **A grep count is not a coverage verdict.** When a count returns zero, establish *which* zero: untested, tested elsewhere, or unused. - **A passing test can encode the bug.** A tie-break suite named "order doesn't change the outcome" used only distinct timestamps — the one arrangement already order-independent. It passed while the bug was live. **The shape all of these share: a proxy reported as the finding.** The standard: **make the check fail on purpose before its pass counts.** If something is asserted rather than proven, say so. --- ## Play 6 — Accessibility WCAG **2.2** AA. Per-component AC: keyboard operable · visible focus · accessible name · correct semantic element · contrast 4.5:1 / 3:1 · **24×24 target size** (2.5.8, a 2.2 addition). **What the tooling misses**, so don't treat a clean run as clearance: the `` ast-grep rule matches `^img$` only and is blind to Chakra's ``; the `IconButton` rule rejects `aria-labelledby` — the more correct answer — because of a word-boundary bug; the clickable-non-interactive rule checks neither `tabIndex` nor `onKeyDown`. All three are `severity: warning`. **Open item:** whether missing alt text should be absent or `alt=""` is a content-model question, not a code one. Needs a decision from Tim. --- ## Play 7 — Page-level validation | Part | Where it lands today | |---|---| | E2E | partial — **one spec file exists in the entire repo** | | Lighthouse | yes, at SIT tier | | **Design parity** | **no automated home — defaults to you** | ⚠️ **No page has a Storybook story**, despite `components.md` requiring one for page-level assemblies. The `@area` vocabulary is `homepage · checkout · search · account · pdp · plp · integrations`. Only `homepage` has a spec, and only `e2e_homepage` is mapped in the change-scoping config — each new area's first spec needs its own allow-list group or it silently falls back to the full suite. Visual regression (Chromatic / Loki / Percy) would give design parity an automated home. It's a new dependency and a budget line, so it needs approval before it's proposed as a plan. --- ## Play 8 — Pushing back before sizing **The Figma link on the card is a build input.** A stale link propagates three ways: the dev builds the wrong thing, the BA signs off against a different frame, QA tests a third source. Ask the BA to fix the card. **Decisions need a findable home.** A decision recorded only in a Teams thread will be re-litigated within a month.

Node type decides whether a measurement is even comparable. - **Value-matching audits produce confident nonsense.** "These 41 literals should be tokens" inflated from 19 by matching `.rem` inside `removeEventListener`. - **A grep count is not a coverage verdict.** When a count returns zero, establish *which* zero: untested, tested elsewhere, or unused. - **A passing test can encode the bug.** A tie-break suite named "order doesn't change the outcome" used only distinct timestamps — the one arrangement already order-independent. It passed while the bug was live. **The shape all of these share: a proxy reported as the finding.** The standard: **make the check fail on purpose before its pass counts.** If something is asserted rather than proven, say so. --- ## Play 6 — Accessibility WCAG **2.2** AA. Per-component AC: keyboard operable · visible focus · accessible name · correct semantic element · contrast 4.5:1 / 3:1 · **24×24 target size** (2.5.8, a 2.2 addition). **What the tooling misses**, so don't treat a clean run as clearance: the `` ast-grep rule matches `^img$` only and is blind to Chakra's ``; the `IconButton` rule rejects `aria-labelledby` — the more correct answer — because of a word-boundary bug; the clickable-non-interactive rule checks neither `tabIndex` nor `onKeyDown`. All three are `severity: warning`. **Open item:** whether missing alt text should be absent or `alt=""` is a content-model question, not a code one. Needs a decision from Tim. --- ## Play 7 — Page-level validation | Part | Where it lands today | |---|---| | E2E | partial — **one spec file exists in the entire repo** | | Lighthouse | yes, at SIT tier | | **Design parity** | **no automated home — defaults to you** | ⚠️ **No page has a Storybook story**, despite `components.md` requiring one for page-level assemblies. The `@area` vocabulary is `homepage · checkout · search · account · pdp · plp · integrations`. Only `homepage` has a spec, and only `e2e_homepage` is mapped in the change-scoping config — each new area's first spec needs its own allow-list group or it silently falls back to the full suite. Visual regression (Chromatic / Loki / Percy) would give design parity an automated home. It's a new dependency and a budget line, so it needs approval before it's proposed as a plan. --- ## Play 8 — Pushing back before sizing **The Figma link on the card is a build input.** A stale link propagates three ways: the dev builds the wrong thing, the BA signs off against a different frame, QA tests a third source. Ask the BA to fix the card. **Decisions need a findable home.** A decision recorded only in a Teams thread will be re-litigated within a month.

# PRD – Product Detail Page (PDP)

*Source of truth: Zimmermann Functional Requirements.xlsx, sheets "Product, Catalogue and PDP" (PRD), "Cart & Inventory" (CAI), "Payments" (PAY), "Returns and Refunds" (RRC), "Customers, Account, CRM Sync" (CRM), "Order Management" (OM). Last updated: 2026-06-19.*

---

## 1. Page Structure

- Breadcrumb navigation displayed on all PDP pages (PRD-001, confirmed)
- Style code (SKU) displayed on PDP (PRD-007, confirmed)
- Key supporting information in expandable accordions: **Details, Size & Fit, Care, Shipping & Free Returns** (region-specific content) (PRD-008, confirmed)

---

## 2. Product Data

- Product name, price, sizes, and colour swatches sourced from the **Product API** (fed from AP21, but AP21 may not be the sole source in future — do not hard-code AP21 as the only data provider). Colour swatch assets do not live in AP21 — only colour names (PRD-002, confirmed — requirement updated for clarity 05.05)
- Style code (SKU) from product data (PRD-007, confirmed)
- "Also available in" / "Only available in" colour swatches; selecting a colour updates the page content and URL (PRD-004, confirmed). Hover-to-preview swatch behaviour (colour updates on rollover without click) is a **custom build, not OOTB, and not scoped for go-live** — see Open Items (PRD-004)
- *Open: product copy ownership (description, editorial text) — Contentful vs SFCC vs AP21 is TBD (see AGENTS.md "Unresolved Dependencies")*

---

## 3. Product Badges & Tags (PRD-005 – PRD-006, confirmed)

- Products can carry one or more badges: **Campaign, Runway, Exclusive, Online Exclusive, VIC Exclusive** — badge *assignment* on applicable products is confirmed (PRD-005)
- Multiple badges per product are supported; a defined display priority/hierarchy applies when more than one badge is present
- Badge creation must not require a code deployment (PRD-005, comment: "ideally the creation of these badges would not require a code change")
- **Badges are clickable** and navigate the customer to a PLP view filtered to products in that badge category (PRD-005, confirmed — workbook updated 2026-06-19: "captured in requirement"). See also plp.md §2.6.
- *Design caveat: badges not yet present in PLP designs ("Missing badges in PLP") (PRD-005)*
