input.description: Read fedLead-playbook closing sections

content.content:
## Who owns what

| Area | Working owner |
|---|---|
| Component conventions, reuse | you |
| Design tokens, Figma sign-off | UI designer |
| Story decomposition | BA, with your input |
| Content model / field IDs | you + Integration |
| CI/CD, env, secrets | Integration / SI |
| Release cut, final tags | tier-1-approvers |
| **Design-parity validation** | **unassigned — defaults to you** |

Run a boundary-setting session rather than discovering these one escalation at a time — and
put design-parity validation on its agenda explicitly. It is the only row with no owner, and an
unresourced ask that quietly becomes yours is the failure mode this table exists to prevent.

---

## Standing artifacts you own

| Artifact | Cadence |
|---|---|
| Component reuse register | per refinement |
| Token gap list | weekly, into design review |
| Estimation re-baseline | once, then per sprint |
| The three docs in this set | after each substantial build |
| Open-decisions list with owners | continuous |

---

## Current open items

1. **Set required reviewers on `prod`/`staging`/`uat`.** Highest-value fix available;
   `rollback=true` is an ungated production bypass until then.
2. **`CODERABBIT_API_KEY` is a plaintext GitHub Actions *variable*** — 61 characters,
   retrievable by any repo collaborator. So are `CONTENTFUL_PREVIEW_TOKEN` (gates draft
   content) and `CONTENTFUL_DELIVERY_TOKEN`. The plaintext-variable mechanism is a documented,
   accepted tradeoff for *public identifiers*; a live API key isn't one.
3. **Provision `LHCI_*` secrets and write one `*.p0.spec`** — until both exist, no release PR
   can merge.
4. **Add `babel.config.js` and `tsconfig.json` to CODEOWNERS.** Declared Tier 1, enforced
   nowhere.
5. **Reconcile `squadA.md`/`squadB.md` with CODEOWNERS**, or retire them. They contradict the
   enforcing artefact on PDP ownership and mostly name paths that don't exist.
6. **Refresh `sprintScope.md`** or remove Hard Rule 14's dependency on it.
6b. **Two skill-layer traps that are still live:** `session-reflect.sh` forbids direct edits to
    `.docs/memory/*` while `session-start` instructs them; and `/code-quality`'s default
    `git diff --name-only main` fails outright in a checkout with no local `main`
    (`/pr-checklist` correctly uses `develop`).
6c. **Terminology collision worth stating once to the team:** `new-component`'s "story" is a
    Storybook file; `qa-generate`'s "story" is a Jira story becoming Gherkin. Same word, two
    unrelated artifacts, two different audiences.
7. **Amend `overrideStyling.md`'s justification for dropping the `.zimm-btn-*` classes.** As
   written it claims a static class *"can't express `_hover`/`_active`/`_disabled`/
   `_focusVisible`"* — **simply untrue of plain CSS**, and anyone who notices can dismiss the
   whole rule. The real reasons are that two surfaces for one component drift, and a class
   can't see the Chakra token layer. The conclusion is right; the stated reason is false.
7b. **Coordinate the F2R conversion before Han's 16 components land.** They sit at
   `ui-kits/{atoms,molecules,organisms}/zimm-button/` (kebab, not camelCase) with co-located
   `<name>.styles.ts`. **Don't discard the `.styles.ts` files** — they're a faithful Figma→CSS
   transcription and good raw material for a recipe. Convert them; don't copy the pattern. That
   branch also predates PR #56 and carries its own `theme/foundation/`, so expect a real
   conflict.
7c. **Settle `ui-kits` vs `uiKits`.** It's currently a silent exception to the camelCase rule.
   Leave it undocumented and the next person adds `ui-kits/form-fields/`.
7d. **Reference `overrideStyling.md` from `AGENTS.md` and add it to
   `scripts/syncCursorRules.mjs`'s manifest.** The largest rules file, holding the entire
   styling hierarchy, is orphaned from the entry-point doc and invisible to Cursor and Copilot.
8. **Triage `audit:tokens`' 19 findings**, then wire it into CI.
9. **`promoteAlias.mjs:70` calls `environmentAlias.createOrUpdate`, which doesn't exist** in
   `contentful-management@12.3.2` — 0 occurrences in the package. The production content
   cutover script throws on its first real run. `bootstrapSpace.mjs:238-240` has the correct
   pattern.
10. **Contentful content model exists only on `dev`.** Four tiers are empty; the template covers
    5 of 14 types; there is no forward content promotion at all.

---

*Revised 25 August 2026 against `develop` @ `8362b3c`. This pass absorbed
`zimmermann_frontend_lead_playbook.md` (§3, §4) and added four sections: working with AI
tooling, release/tagging/promotion, sprint & Jira/Confluence, and integration boundaries.
Governance was expanded from a paragraph to a section after verification showed the rules files
and `CODEOWNERS` disagree on several paths — and that `CODEOWNERS`, which has no catch-all
rule, is the one that decides.*

content.text:
I have what I need. Agent 1 hasn't reported, but I covered its material items independently.

## 1. Conflicts and omissions — most actionable first

**A. CONFLICT — the hardcoded `Style Code:` label directly reverses the takeover report's named remediation, and the test that guarded it was deleted**

The report's §7 "safe to do right now" item 4: *"Route four strings through `react-intl` … `pdpProductInfo:59` (`Style Code:`) … `useIntl` is already imported."* §10 escalates it: *"A hardcoded English literal is the same class of defect as a hardcoded hex. Four shipped on this PR."*

`/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa/overrides/app/components/ui-kits/atoms/zimmProductStyleCode/index.tsx:9` — `const LABEL = 'Style Code:';`. Three things make this worse than #57's version:
- The in-file justification (`:22-25`) argues only against *Contentful* microcopy ("`useContentful.ts` requests entries with no `locale` parameter") — which is correct and is a real finding from the docs. It never addresses `react-intl`, which both files this branch ports use throughout, and which the branch already calls in the same subtree (`partials/staticProductHeader.tsx:48`).
- An earlier working state (off-branch commit `3ae8dcd`, never pushed, not an ancestor of HEAD) *did* use `useUiCopy` with a fallback. Commit `57cd0b9` removed it. Because the removal happened off-branch, `git diff develop..HEAD` shows only the hardcoded end state — **invisible to any PR-diff review.**
- The same commit deleted the one mechanical check that the label wasn't inlined: a test named `'takes the label from useUiCopy, not a hardcoded string'`, which asserted a Spanish CMS override won over the fallback. Its removal is recorded only as a lint-*warning*-count delta in the commit body ("the warning baseline drops from 16 because the CMS-override test and its now-unused import are both gone").

The styling and override layer is clean against every trap the docs name: all seven recipes are namespaced `Zimm*`, registered in `theme/components/index.ts`, and — checked individually — actually consumed, so none is a dead registered recipe. # LOCAL-DOCS CONFORMANCE AUDIT — SFCC-89 @ `3920caf`

**Verdict up front:** on the subject these docs mostly cover — override mechanics, recipe/token discipline, Chakra's silent failure modes — this branch is clean, and materially more conformant than PR #57. The real conflicts are concentrated in three places the styling docs *don't* cover: **i18n, requirements-gating, and takeover/process.** Ranked below by what a reviewer would act on.

I re-ran `audit:tokens`, `tsc --noEmit` and `npm run lint` rather than trusting the commit bodies, and made one of my own hypotheses fail on purpose (see §5).

---

## 1. Conflicts and omissions, most actionable first

### 1.1 CONFLICT — the hardcoded label moved *away* from the remedy the takeover report named

**Doc** (PR57 report §7, item 4 — "Safe to do right now"):
> "Route four strings through `react-intl` | `breadcrumb:51` (`aria-label`), `:55` (`Home`), **`pdpProductInfo:59` (`Style Code:`)**, `product-detail:66` (the error text). `useIntl` is already imported."

**Doc** (PR57 report §10, Med-high):
> "**No i18n rule exists anywhere**, on a project with 11 locales | Add one: every user-facing string through `react-intl` — copy, `aria-label`s, `alt` text, errors... **A hardcoded English literal is the same class of defect as a hardcoded hex.**"

**Code** — `/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa/overrides/app/components/ui-kits/atoms/zimmProductStyleCode/index.tsx:9`:
```ts
const LABEL = 'Style Code:';
```
Commit `57cd0b9`: *"The style code label no longer goes through useUiCopy."*

**Verdict: CONFLICT — and this is the single most actionable item.** The build's *diagnosis* is correct and well-sourced (`useContentful.ts` passes no `locale`, so a `uiCopy` lookup serves one space default to all eight storefronts — independently documented in `uiBuild-knowledge.md` §8). But the *conclusion* inverts the instruction: the fix for a locale-blind lookup is the localisation mechanism the report named, not removing localisation. There was no structural barrier — `useIntl` is available and this very build calls it in `/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa/overrides/app/pages/product-detail/partials/staticProductHeader.tsx`, and `components.md`'s documented exception permits `useIntl` from a presentational leaf.

Aggravating: the commit also **deleted the test that proved the label was sourced**, so the branch removed the one mechanical check on this string in the same commit that hardcoded it (`57cd0b9` body: *"the warning baseline drops from 16 because the CMS-override test and its now-unused import are both gone"*).

**Action:** route `LABEL` through `formatMessage`; raise the message id (`translations/` is Tier 2 — request, don't edit).

---

### 1.2 CONFLICT — hard-codes a data source that two repo docs mark unresolved

**Doc** — `/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa/.docs/prd/pdp.md:20`:
> "*Open: product copy ownership (description, editorial text) — Contentful vs SFCC vs AP21 is TBD (see AGENTS.md "Unresolved Dependencies")*"

**Doc** — `/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa/.docs/memory/projectState.md:104`:
> "Do not hard-code assumptions for the following — ask the user before implementing: Product copy ownership: Contentful vs SFCC vs AP21 (TBD)."

**Doc** (`fedLead-playbook.md`): *"an **invented data source** is a story problem, not a code problem — fix the story."*

**Code** — `overrides/app/pages/product-detail/productInfo.ts:59`: `description: product.longDescription` — commits to SFCC as the copy source.

**Verdict: CONFLICT.** PR57 report §5 already charged #57 with a requirements defect here (`shortDescription || longDescription` as a guess). This build removes the guess but still picks a side on an item flagged "ask the user before implementing."

Related, and worth noting because it's cheap: **no commit body cites `.docs/` or a PRD id at all.** They cite `.claude/rules/` files, Figma node ids, and base line numbers — thoroughly — but AGENTS.md's Requirements section asks for the doc/section up front, and `PRD-007` (style code) is right there and confirmed.

**Action:** raise with the BA; record the interim choice on the story rather than only in a type comment.

---

### 1.3 OMISSION — the four E2E artifacts #57 delivered were discarded, not carried forward

**Doc** (PR57 report §4, crediting #57): *"gherkin-first followed, the `.feature` file exists"*
**Doc** (PR57 report §10, takeover guidance): *"preserve their artifacts as raw material"*
**Doc** (`.claude/rules/testing.md` pre-PR checklist): *"New user journey → has a `.feature` file"*

**Evidence.** PR #57's branch shipped four files this branch does not:
```
e2e/features/pdp/SFCC-89_pdp-static-product-information.feature
e2e/fixtures/products.js
e2e/support/pages/ProductPage.js
e2e/tests/zimm/pdp/SFCC-89_pdp-static-product-information.spec.js
```
`git diff develop..HEAD --name-only | grep -E 'e2e|\.feature|\.spec'` → empty. `e2e/features/` on this branch contains only `homepage`.

**Verdict: OMISSION.** Compounding: `origin/feature/SFCC-91_...` carries those same four files forward, so merging SFCC-89 without them makes SFCC-91's rebase worse, not better. And this is invisible to CI by design — per `testing.md`, with no `@SFCC-89`-tagged spec, `e2e-browserstack`'s `--grep` matches zero tests and reports success. A missing spec is a silent free pass.

**Action:** port the `.feature` and `ProductPage.js` across, or state in the PR body that E2E is deferred and to which ticket.

---

### 1.4 CONFLICT — takeover sequencing: rebuilt from `develop` instead of adopting; the SFCC-91 conflict is now larger

**Doc** (PR57 report §6, Decision 4):
> "**SFCC-91 (colour swatches) already branched off SFCC-89 at an older commit** and carries ~650 lines plus an 883-line spec. Rebasing it will conflict in the product-info component. **Adopt that work, don't rewrite it**, and tell Jhoan before you convert anything."

**Doc** (PR57 report §5): *"It's orderly, traceable code sitting one level too low. **Finish it, don't restart it.**"* / §11: *"**Day 1–2 — finish what he started.**"*

**Evidence.**
- `git merge-base --is-ancestor origin/feature/SFCC-89_pdp-ui-static-product-information HEAD` → **false**. Branch renamed (`..._pdp-static-product-info`), no upstream, never pushed, shares no ancestry with #57.
- Zero swatch/colour commits adopted.
- SFCC-91 is **24 commits** past its fork point and touches three files this branch rewrites: `overrides/app/pages/product-detail/index.tsx`, `overrides/app/routes.tsx`, `overrides/app/types/vendor.d.ts`.
- The page went **48 → 936 lines**, so the conflict surface is an order of magnitude bigger than when the report was written.

**Verdict: CONFLICT on process, not on architecture.** The rebuild *is* the report's recommended Decision-1(b) "Compose" shape, and it's substantively better than #57 (see §2). The conflict is with the adopt-and-finish instruction and the "tell the author first" step, and with the fact that nobody has yet decided which branch rebases onto which.

**Action:** coordinate with the SFCC-91 owner **before** merge, and record the direction.

---

### 1.5 CONFLICT — the absent-value guard sits at the page selector, not at the atom

**Doc** (`uiBuild-knowledge.md` §7):
> "An empty-string fallback is a layout bug — `heading ?? ''` renders an empty element that **keeps its margins**... **Fix at the atom**, not at each call site."

**Doc** (PR57 report §7, item 3): *"Fix it **in the component**, not with the page's `?? ''`."*

**DOC STALE — `uiBuild-knowledge.md` names this build's files as live violations, and they're fixed.** It says: *"**Live violations right now:** `ui-kits/atoms/zimmProductName/index.tsx:20` and `zimmProductModelInfo/index.tsx:23` both use `color="text.default"`."* At `3920caf` neither file has a `color=` prop; colour moved into the recipes. The doc was measured against an intermediate working tree ("18 in the current working tree, which adds four uncommitted product-view recipes"). Worth correcting so it doesn't get cited against clean code.

**DOC STALE — two of the secondary sources shouldn't be treated as binding.** `zimmermann_frontend_lead_playbook.md` was **retired 25 Aug** and absorbed into `fedLead-playbook.md` (§3, §4) — it self-declares this. `development-workflows-difference-with-pwa-kit.md` describes Storefront Next / Vite / `sfnext dev`, a different product from this repo's webpack PWA Kit; not applicable.

**Falsification I ran on myself.** I hypothesised that `staticProductHeader.tsx:58`'s `mr={4} spacing={2} marginBottom={[4,4,4,0,0]}` would silently misresolve, since `overrides/app/theme/index.ts:56` does `space: spacing` and the Zimmermann scale has only named keys. **Wrong.** `extendTheme` deep-merges, so Chakra's numerics survive — and `overrides/app/theme/index.test.tsx:62` already asserts exactly this (`test('space carries the named Zimmermann scale and keeps Chakra numerics')`, `expect(theme.space[4]).toBeTruthy()`). Measured: `space[4] = "1rem"`, `sizes[64] = "16rem"`, `sizes.m = undefined`. The numeric spacing is safe, and it's safe because of a real pre-existing guard rather than luck. Recording the dead end because the docs' own standard is that a check has to be made to fail before its pass counts.
